p.src: After Feng Ziying had left, Jia Zheng summoned one of the gatekeepers and asked, “The Earl of Lin’an has invited us to a feast today. Do you know what the occasion is?” The gatekeeper replied, “I took the liberty of asking, but there is no particular celebration. It is only that a troupe of young actors has arrived at the Prince of Nan’an’s residence, and everyone says it is a renowned company. His Lordship is in high spirits and means to stage plays for two days, inviting the gentlemen with whom he is friendly to come and enjoy the entertainment. Most likely, there will be no need to send a gift.” As he spoke, Jia She came over and asked, “Will you be going tomorrow, Second Brother?” Jia Zheng replied, “Since he has shown us such cordiality, how could I well refuse?” While he was speaking, a gatekeeper entered and reported, “A clerk from the yamen has come to ask Your Lordship to attend tomorrow. There is a case assigned for hearing, so you must go early.” “Very well,” said Jia Zheng. Just then, two household servants who managed the collection of rents from the estate lands came in, paid their respects, kowtowed, and stood to one side. Jia Zheng asked, “Are you men from Hao Family Village?” The two men answered that they were. Jia Zheng questioned them no further, but chatted awhile with Jia She; then the two brothers went their separate ways. The servants carried hand lanterns and escorted Jia She back.

p.src: Jia Lian then said to the rent collector, “Now tell me your business.” The man said, “I have already sent the rents for the tenth month on their way, and they were due to arrive tomorrow. But outside the capital, officials were requisitioning carts, and without so much as a word they threw everything from ours onto the ground. I told them that these were carts carrying rents to this mansion, not commercial wagons. But they paid no attention whatever. I told the drivers to keep going, whereupon several runners set upon them indiscriminately, beat them soundly, and forcibly dragged away two carts. That is why I came ahead to report it. I beg you to send someone to the yamen to reclaim the carts. And it would be well to teach those lawless runners a lesson too. You do not know the worst of it, sir. The commercial carriers are even more to be pitied: the officials care nothing for the merchants’ goods, but dump them out and drive the carts away. If any driver says a single word, they beat him until his head is split and bleeding.” Hearing this, Jia Lian cursed, “This is outrageous!” He immediately wrote a note and ordered a servant, “Take this to the yamen responsible for the requisitions and demand the return of the carts and everything that was on them. If even one article is missing, I shall not let the matter rest. Quickly, summon Zhou Rui.” Zhou Rui was not at home. He then called for Wang’er, but Wang’er had gone out at noon and had not yet returned. “Those little bastards!” exclaimed Jia Lian. “Not one of them is at home! They draw their keep all year round and never attend to any business.” He ordered the pages, “Go and find them at once.” With that, he returned to his own rooms and went to bed. We shall leave him there.

p.src: The next day, the Earl of Lin’an again sent someone with an invitation. Jia Zheng told Jia She, “I have business at the yamen, and Lian must remain at home awaiting news of the requisitioned carts, so he cannot go either. You had better take Baoyu and represent us for the day, Elder Brother.” Jia She nodded. “That will do.” Jia Zheng sent for Baoyu and told him, “Today you are to accompany your elder uncle to the Earl of Lin’an’s residence to see the plays.” Baoyu was overjoyed. He changed his clothes and came out with his three young attendants, Beiming, Saohong, and Chuyao. After paying his respects to Jia She, he entered the carriage, and they proceeded to the Earl of Lin’an’s residence. The gatekeeper went in to announce them and returned after a moment, saying, “His Lordship asks you to enter.” Jia She led Baoyu into the courtyard, where they found the guests gathered in noisy profusion. Jia She and Baoyu paid their respects to the Earl of Lin’an and exchanged courtesies with all the other guests. Everyone sat talking and laughing for a while. Presently, the troupe manager appeared carrying a playbill and an ivory tablet. He made a respectful salute before the company and said, “May Your Lordships be pleased to choose the plays.” He began with the most honored guest and proceeded down the company until he reached Jia She, who also chose a piece. Turning and catching sight of Baoyu, the man went no farther but hurried over, saluted him, and said, “Second Master, please favor us by choosing two pieces.” When Baoyu looked at him, he saw a face as though dusted with powder, lips as if painted with vermilion, fresh and lustrous as a lotus newly risen from the water, and graceful as a jade tree swaying in the wind. It was none other than Jiang Yuhan. Baoyu had recently heard that Jiang Yuhan had brought a troupe of young actors to the capital, yet Jiang had not visited him. Now that he saw him, Baoyu could hardly rise in such company and merely smiled. “When did you arrive?” Jiang Yuhan pointed to himself with one hand and replied with a smile, “How is it that Second Master does not know?” Since all the others were present, Baoyu could not speak freely and had to choose a play at random. After Jiang Yuhan had gone, several guests began discussing him. “Who is that man?” they asked. One replied, “He used to specialize in young female roles. Now he no longer wishes to play them, and he is older too, so he manages the troupe at the residence. He had earlier switched to young male roles as well. He has saved a considerable sum and already owns two or three shops, but he refuses to abandon his profession and continues to lead the troupe as before.” Another said, “I suppose he has married by now.” Someone else replied, “His marriage has not even been arranged. He has made up his mind that choosing a spouse is a matter affecting one’s whole life and must not be treated lightly. Highborn or lowborn, rich or poor, she must in every case be a match for his own talents. That is why he remains unmarried to this day.” Baoyu thought to himself, “I wonder whose daughter will marry him one day. Any girl who marries such a gifted and handsome man may count herself fortunate indeed.”

p.src: After noon had passed, the tables were laid and the guests began drinking. After watching for a while longer, Jia She made ready to leave. The Earl of Lin'an came over to detain him. “It is still early. I hear Jiang Yuhan has another piece, The Courtesan Queen, one of their finest specialties.” At this, Baoyu fervently hoped Jia She would not leave. Jia She therefore remained seated a while longer. Sure enough, Jiang Yuhan, playing Young Qin, portrayed his tender attendance upon the drunken Courtesan Queen, expressing the utmost delicacy and devotion of one who cherishes beauty. Afterward they drank and sang to each other, lingering in tender intimacy. By then Baoyu was no longer watching the Courtesan Queen; both his eyes were fixed solely upon Young Qin. Jiang Yuhan's voice was resonant, his diction crisp, and every phrase and beat perfectly judged; Baoyu's very soul was drawn into his singing. Only when the performers had left the stage did Baoyu understand more fully that Jiang Yuhan was a man of the deepest feeling, far beyond any common actor. He recalled the words of the Record of Music: “When emotion stirs within, it takes form in sound. When sounds assume patterned form, they are called music.” Thus there was much subtle learning involved in understanding sound, understanding tone, and understanding music. The source of sound must be carefully examined. Poetry could convey emotion but could not penetrate to the bone; from then on, he resolved to study musical principles more deeply. Baoyu was lost in thought when he suddenly saw Jia She rise; the host had no time to detain him. Baoyu had no choice but to follow him home. On reaching home, Jia She returned to his own quarters, while Baoyu went to see Jia Zheng.

p.src: Jia Zheng had only just returned from his office and was questioning Jia Lian about the seizure of the cart. Jia Lian said, “Today one of our retainers took our card there, but the magistrate was not at home. His gatekeeper said, ‘His Honor knows nothing of this. No official warrant was issued to seize any cart; it was all the doing of those scoundrels, who ran wild outside and tried to extort money. Since it belongs to your lordship's household, I shall send men after them at once. I guarantee that by tomorrow both cart and goods will be delivered here together. If there is the slightest delay, report it again to His Honor and he will punish them severely. As His Honor is away just now, we beg your lordship to overlook the matter; it would be better still if His Honor need never hear of it.’” Jia Zheng said, “If there was no official warrant, then what sort of men were causing this mischief?” “You do not know, sir,” replied Jia Lian. “That is how things are everywhere outside. I expect they will certainly return everything tomorrow.” Having finished his report, Jia Lian withdrew, and Baoyu went forward to pay his respects. After asking him a few questions, Jia Zheng told him to go to the Old Lady's quarters.

p.src: Because none of the household servants had answered Jia Lian's summons the previous night, he came out and called for them; by then most were assembled and waiting. After giving them a scolding, Jia Lian called the chief steward, Lai Sheng. “Bring me the name registers for every department and check them over carefully. Write out a notice so they all understand: anyone who goes out without requesting leave, cannot be found when summoned, and thereby delays official business is to be beaten at once and driven out!” Lai Sheng hastily answered “Yes” several times, then went out and issued the orders. Every servant thereafter took care to be on his guard.

p.src: Our families have long been bound by friendship, and the affection between us has ever been profound. From afar I look toward your lordship's carriage curtains, unable to contain my longing and devotion. Through my poor abilities I incurred punishment and believed that even ten thousand deaths could not atone for my offense. Happily I received merciful pardon and now await judgment on the frontier; yet by this time my household has fallen into decline and its servants are scattered. As for my servant Bao Yong, he was formerly in my employ. Though he possesses no remarkable skill, he is honest and dependable. Should he be allowed to serve on errands and thereby earn his livelihood, I would be boundlessly grateful for the affection that extends even from the householder to the crow upon his roof. I write expressly to convey this request; all else must await another letter. I shall write no more.

p.src: When Jia Zheng had finished reading, he smiled and said, “We already have too many people here, yet the Zhen family has recommended another man to us, and it would hardly do to refuse him.” He instructed the gatekeepers, “Have him come in to see me. Let him stay here for the time being, and we shall employ him according to his abilities.” The gatekeeper went out and brought the man in. At the sight of Jia Zheng, the man knocked his head three times, then rose and said, “My master sends his respects to you, sir.” He then made another formal bow and said, “Bao Yong pays his respects to you, sir.” Jia Zheng asked after Master Zhen and then looked Bao Yong up and down. Bao Yong stood a little over five feet tall, with broad, heavy shoulders, thick eyebrows, bulging eyes, a jutting brow, and a long beard. His complexion was dark and coarse, and he stood with his hands hanging at his sides. Jia Zheng asked, “Have you always served in the Zhen household, or have you only been there a few years?” Bao Yong replied, “I have always served the Zhen family.” “Then why do you wish to leave now?” asked Jia Zheng. Bao Yong replied, “I was unwilling to leave at first. But my master repeatedly ordered me to go, saying, ‘You refuse to serve anywhere else, but in this master’s household you may consider yourself still at home.’ That is why I came.” Jia Zheng said, “Your master should never have become embroiled in such an affair and been brought to his present pass.” Bao Yong said, “I would not normally dare speak of it, but our master is simply too good. He treats everyone with perfect sincerity, and that is precisely what brought trouble upon him.” “Sincerity is the finest quality of all,” said Jia Zheng. Bao Yong replied, “Because he is too sincere, no one likes him; indeed, they find him tiresome.” Jia Zheng smiled and said, “If that is so, Heaven will surely not fail him.” Bao Yong was about to say more when Jia Zheng asked, “I have heard that the young master of your house is also called Baoyu—is that not so?” “Yes,” replied Bao Yong. Jia Zheng asked, “Does he apply himself and strive to advance?” Bao Yong replied, “If you ask about our young master, sir, there is a remarkable story to tell. His nature is just like my master’s: he too is entirely honest and sincere. From childhood he did nothing but play with the girls. His father and mother gave him several severe beatings, but he never changed. The year his mother went to the capital, he fell gravely ill. He was dead for half a day, and his father nearly died of anxiety; even his burial clothes had been prepared. Fortunately, he later recovered. He said that he had gone to an ornamental gateway, where a girl led him into a temple. There he saw many cabinets, and inside them a great many registers. Then he entered a room and saw countless women, many of whom, he said, turned into monsters, while some became skeletons. Terrified beyond endurance, he began to weep and cry out. When my master realized that he had regained consciousness, he immediately summoned treatment, and the boy gradually recovered.

p.src: My master still told him to go and play with the girls, but his disposition had completely changed. He abandoned all the amusements he had once enjoyed and devoted himself solely to his studies. No matter who tried to tempt him, he remained entirely unmoved. By now he has gradually become able to help my master manage some household affairs.” Jia Zheng reflected in silence for a while, then said, “Go and rest for now. p.src: One morning, just as Jia Zheng was about to leave for his office, he saw the gatekeepers whispering among themselves. They seemed eager for him to know something, yet dared not report it openly and merely kept muttering together. Jia Zheng summoned them and asked, “What is the matter with you? Why are you behaving so furtively?” The gatekeepers replied, “We servants dare not say.” “What could possibly have happened that you dare not mention?” asked Jia Zheng. One of the gatekeepers said, “When we rose this morning and opened the gate, we found a sheet of white paper pasted outside, covered with a great many scandalous words.” Jia Zheng said, “How can such a thing be? What does it say?” The gatekeeper replied, “It is filthy gossip about Water-Moon Convent.” “Bring it here and let me see it,” said Jia Zheng. The gatekeeper said, “We meant to tear it down, but it was pasted so firmly that we could not remove it. We had no choice but to copy it while washing it away. Just now, Li De brought me a sheet he had managed to peel off. It bears the same words as those pasted on our gate. We dared not conceal the matter from you.” As he spoke, he presented the copied notice. Jia Zheng took it and read the following:

One of the gatekeepers said, “When we rose this morning and opened the gate, we found a sheet of white paper pasted outside, covered with a great many scandalous words.”

The gatekeeper replied, “It is filthy gossip about Water-Moon Convent.”
“Bring it here and let me see it,” said Jia Zheng.
The gatekeeper said, “We meant to tear it down, but it was pasted so firmly that we could not remove it. We had no choice but to copy it while washing it away.
Just now, Li De brought me a sheet he had managed to peel off. It bears the same words as those pasted on our gate.
We dared not conceal the matter from you.”
As he spoke, he presented the copied notice.
Jia Zheng took it and read the following:

p.src: Jia Lian hurried over at once. Jia Zheng promptly asked him, “Have you ever investigated the Buddhist and Taoist nuns lodging at Water-Moon Convent?” “No,” replied Jia Lian. Qin has always been in charge of them.” Jia Zheng asked, “Do you know whether Qin is capable of managing the place properly?” Jia Lian replied, “Since you put the question that way, sir, I suppose there must be something improper in Qin’s conduct.” Jia Zheng sighed. “Look and see what is written on this notice.” Jia Lian looked at it and exclaimed, “Can such a thing really have happened?” As they were speaking, Jia Rong arrived carrying a letter inscribed, “Confidentially submitted to the Second Master.” When they opened it, they found another anonymous broadside bearing the same words as the notices pasted on the gate. Jia Zheng said, “Tell Lai Da at once to take three or four carts to Water-Moon Convent and bring back every one of those Buddhist and Taoist nuns. Let no word of this leak out. Say only that they have been summoned by the ladies of the inner apartments.” Lai Da received the order and departed.

p.src: Now, when the young Buddhist nuns and Taoist girls first arrived at Water-Moon Convent, the novices and Taoists were placed under the old abbess's supervision, and during the day she taught them sutras and penitential rites. Later, when the Imperial Consort no longer required their services, they grew lax in their studies. As the girls gradually grew older, they began to understand the ways of the world. Jia Qin, moreover, was a libertine. Supposing that Fangguan and the others had taken religious vows merely out of childish whim, he began making advances to them. But Fangguan's resolve proved genuine, and when he could make no headway with her, he transferred his attentions to the young nuns and Taoist girls. Among the young novices was one named Qinxiang, and among the Taoist girls one called Hexian. Both were exceedingly alluring, and Jia Qin soon entered into an affair with them. In their leisure hours they learned to play stringed instruments and sing songs. It was now the middle of the tenth month. After collecting the monthly allowances for the convent's inmates, Jia Qin devised a scheme and told them, “I cannot return to the city after collecting your monthly money, so I shall have to spend the night here. It is bitterly cold—what shall we do? I brought some fruit and wine today. Shall we eat, drink, and make merry all night?” The girls were delighted and set out tables, inviting even the nuns who ordinarily lived at the convent; Fangguan alone refused to come. After several cups, Jia Qin proposed that they play a drinking game. Qinxiang and the others said, “We do not know any drinking games. We had better play finger-guessing instead. Whoever loses must drink a cup—would that not be livelier?” One of the convent's nuns said, “It is only just past noon. It would hardly be proper to start shouting and drinking wildly now. Let us first have a few cups, and whoever wishes to leave may go. Later tonight, those who want to keep Master Qin company may drink as much as they please; I shall not interfere.” As she spoke, an old Taoist woman hurried in and cried, “Disperse at once! Steward Lai from the mansion is here.” The nuns hurriedly cleared everything away and told Jia Qin to hide. Having drunk several cups too many, Jia Qin declared, “I came to deliver their monthly allowances. What have I to fear?” Before he had finished, Lai Da entered. The sight before him filled him with fury. But Jia Zheng had ordered him not to make the matter public, so he could only conceal his feelings behind a vague smile and say, “Why, Master Qin, are you here too?” Jia Qin sprang to his feet and asked, “Steward Lai, what brings you here?” Lai Da replied, “It is even better that you are here, sir. Tell the novices and Taoists to pack at once, board the carts, and return to the city. They have been summoned by the Palace.” Jia Qin and the others did not know the reason and wanted to question him further. But Lai Da said, “It is already late. We must hurry if we are to reach the city in time.” The girls had no choice but to board the carts together, while Lai Da mounted a large fast mule and escorted them into the city. But no more of this for now.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Jia Zheng learned of the affair, he was so enraged that he could not even report to his office and sat alone sighing in his inner study. Jia Lian did not dare leave either. Presently a gatekeeper came in and reported, “Master Zhang is assigned to duty at the office tonight, but as he has fallen ill, a notice has arrived asking you, sir, to take his shift.” Jia Zheng had been waiting for Lai Da to return so that he could deal with Jia Qin; now that he was also required to go on duty, he felt thoroughly vexed and said nothing. Jia Lian stepped forward and said, “Lai Da left after the meal. Water-Moon Convent is more than twenty li from the city, so even if he hurries back, it will be the second watch before he arrives. Since you have been called to substitute tonight, please go without concern. When Lai Da returns, I shall have him keep them under guard and make no commotion. You can deal with them tomorrow after you return. If Qin comes back as well, we need not explain anything to him. Let us see what he has to say when he faces you tomorrow.” Jia Zheng saw the sense in this and had no choice but to go on duty.

p.src: Jia Lian at last found a chance to return to his own rooms. As he walked, he inwardly blamed Xifeng for the scheme she had proposed and wanted to reproach her; but since she was ill, he had to restrain himself and walked on slowly. Meanwhile, the servants passed the news from one to ten until it reached the inner apartments. Ping'er was the first there to hear of it and hurried to tell Xifeng. Xifeng had been unwell since that night and remained listless and dispirited; just then she was worrying about the affair at Iron-Threshold Temple. When she heard that an anonymous placard had been posted outside, she started in alarm and hastily asked what had been written on it. Ping'er answered without thinking and inadvertently misspoke: “It is nothing serious. It concerns Steamed-Bun Convent.” Already burdened by a guilty conscience, Xifeng was so terrified at the words “Steamed-Bun Convent” that she froze, unable to utter a word. The sudden shock sent the blood surging upward; her vision blurred, and after a fit of coughing she gave a cry and spat out a mouthful of blood. Ping'er panicked and said, “The affair at Water-Moon Convent is merely about the young nuns and Taoist girls. Why should you upset yourself, madam?” Hearing that it was Water-Moon Convent, Xifeng composed herself a little and said, “Pah, you muddle-headed creature! Is it Water-Moon Convent or Steamed-Bun Convent?” Ping'er laughed. “At first I mistakenly heard that it was Steamed-Bun Convent, but later I learned that it was not Steamed-Bun Convent at all—it was Water-Moon Convent. Just now my tongue slipped, and I called it Steamed-Bun Convent again.” “I knew it was Water-Moon Convent,” said Xifeng. “What has Steamed-Bun Convent to do with me? After all, I was the one who put Qin in charge of Water-Moon Convent. He has probably been withholding their monthly allowances.” Ping'er said, “From what I heard, it does not sound like a matter of monthly allowances. There was some filthy talk as well.” Xifeng said, “That concerns me even less. Where has your Second Master gone?” Ping'er replied, “He heard that the master was angry and dared not leave. When I heard that the matter was serious, I ordered the servants not to make a commotion. I do not know whether the ladies have heard yet. All I heard was that the master ordered Lai Da to seize those girls. We should send someone to the front to find out what is happening. Since you are ill, madam, I think you should leave their affairs alone for now.” While they were speaking, Jia Lian came in. Xifeng was about to question him, but seeing the anger on his face, she pretended for the time being to know nothing. Before Jia Lian had finished his meal, Wang'er came and said, “You are wanted outside, sir. Lai Da has returned.” “Has Qin returned?” Jia Lian asked. “He has,” replied Wang'er. Jia Lian said, “Go and tell Lai Da that the master has gone to his official duty. Have those girls confined in the Garden for the time being. Tomorrow, when the master returns, they can be sent into the Palace. Only tell Qin to wait for me in the inner study.” Wang'er departed.

p.src: Jia Qin entered the study and saw the servants pointing and gesturing, though he could not tell what they were saying. From the look of things, it did not seem that the palace wanted anyone. He thought of asking someone, but could get nothing out of them. While he stood there puzzled, Jia Lian came out. Jia Qin paid his respects, then stood deferentially with his hands at his sides and said, “I do not know why Her Ladyship has suddenly summoned those children to the palace. It gave your nephew quite a rush. Luckily, I had come to deliver their monthly allowance today and had not yet left, so I came here with Lai Da. I expect you know the reason, Second Uncle.” “What would I know?” said Jia Lian. “You are the one who knows all about it!” Jia Qin could make neither head nor tail of this and dared not ask again. Jia Lian said, “A fine thing you have done! You have made the master furious.” “Your nephew has done nothing,” said Jia Qin. “The convent receives its allowance every month, and the children never neglect the sutras and penitential rites.” Seeing that he truly knew nothing, and remembering how they often joked together, Jia Lian sighed. “You wretched fool—you had better see for yourself!” He took the anonymous placard from inside his boot and tossed it to him. Jia Qin picked it up and read it. His face turned ashen with fright. “Who did this?” he cried. “I have offended no one. Why would anyone try to ruin me like this? “I go there only once a month to deliver the money. None of these things ever happened. “If the master returns and has me beaten and questioned, I shall die. “If my mother learns of it, she will surely beat me to death too.” As he spoke, he saw that no one else was nearby, dropped to his knees, and pleaded, “Dear Uncle, please save me!” He kept kowtowing as tears streamed from his eyes. Jia Lian thought, “The master detests such things above all. If an inquiry proves that any of this happened, his anger will be terrible. “It would also disgrace us if word got out, and only encourage whoever posted that placard. “Besides, there will be plenty of business of our own to attend to in future. “Better to take advantage of the master’s being at his office and consult with Lai Da. If we can muddle through this, the whole affair may come to nothing. “At present there are no witnesses to confront him.” Having made up his mind, he said, “Do not try to hide it from me. You imagine I know nothing of the furtive things you have been doing. “If you want this matter settled, then even if the master has you beaten and questioned, you must firmly insist that nothing happened. “Shameless wretch, get up!” He sent someone to summon Lai Da. Before long, Lai Da arrived. Jia Lian discussed the matter with him. Lai Da said, “Master Qin’s behavior truly has been outrageous. “When your servant reached the convent today, they were drinking there. “The things written on that placard must certainly have happened.” Jia Lian said, “Listen to that, Qin. Surely Lai Da would not falsely accuse you.” Jia Qin’s face flushed crimson, and he dared not say a word.
